cells.tense: You are standing with the thing that needs holding, and the first clear sight of it is arriving now.
cells.ask: Say out loud the first thing you notice about the thing in your hands, before acting on it — one sentence, to whoever is there.
cells.core:
You can carry something and take in what it actually is in the same pass. The first clean impression arrives while you're already bearing it, and nothing in you flinches from what you see or rushes to smooth it into something easier to live with. You catch the shape before anyone puts a name on it.

Holding steady and paying attention are one motion in you, not two. Your stance, your breath, your look — they don't fire as separate steps, and the look doesn't need defending once it lands. The ask is to speak the first thing you notice before you do anything about it. What comes next gets to answer what's actually there, not what you braced for.
cells.sheetLine: You hold the thing and take it in at once.
cells.verb: catching the first shape of a thing before it has a name
cells.place: where you stand and hold what has to be held

cells.tense: You will brace under a weight that hasn't arrived, and you'll catch its shape long before you meet it.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've already decided how it will go and leave it undecided today. Don't prepare for either version. Let it stay open.
cells.core:
You've already caught the shape of something that hasn't happened. How it goes, what it costs, where it stings — you're holding that picture the way you'd hold the thing itself, and the bracing spends you on a load that may not show. The arrival, when it comes, will be lighter than the one you rehearsed.

On a good day, what you catch stays fresh on what's actually in the room — no run-through, no pre-written lines. The ask is to leave one thing open today. You called how it turns out; un-call it and don't practice either ending. What's here will come on its own schedule, and you'll still be in it when it does.

cells.tense: You were braced at a door that has since closed, and you are still standing at the same spot.
cells.ask: Choose one small thing with a clear end and finish it today. Small is fine. Just finish it.
cells.core:
On a good day, you take in what's here and let it land, and you finish what you start. Right now neither is happening. Things arrive without really landing, and you set them down before they're done. You've been holding a position rather than holding ground.

What puts the floor back is picking one small thing with a clear end and finishing it. That's all. A finished thing is something you can stand on, and standing on something is how the ground returns — not because finishing proves anything, but because a piece with an end gives what you catch next somewhere to land.

cells.tense: You are already catching what's arriving, and you describe it as though it showed up on its own.
cells.ask: Name one thing you noticed before anyone said it — say "I saw that," not "it came up," just once.
cells.core:
The first look is already happening — you catch what's coming before it has a label, and you hold it long enough to see it. That's real, and it shapes what you do next. But the way you put it, the situation showed itself, or you were just being sensible. The look was yours and you keep handing it off.

What's underneath the whole picture is simpler: you're the place the new thing enters, and you're already there for it. Give one instance back to whoever made it. Next time you catch something before anyone names it, tell someone you saw it. Not a claim about who you are — one observation, handed back to the person who made it.
